page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core and multi-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a multi-core score of 16603.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. Image processing and text processing benchmarks also rank in the top 25 percent. However, memory subsystem tests show a weak Passmark memory score of 1572.37, placing in the bottom 25 percent. Large-scale language model inference is a notable bottleneck, with text generation for a 70B model scoring in the bottom 10 percent at 2.45 tokens per second, though smaller 135M model text generation is strong at 296.69 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and large bundled NVMe SSD storage provide high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without requiring external storage attachments. This hardware profile is suited for memory-optimized databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications that require substantial RAM and fast local scratch space, though it is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-sensitive workloads or large-scale language model inference.
